method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)' (last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review')), 21 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 ('Information on the eviQ website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 license (CC BY-NC 4.0).') (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100) 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy' (published online 28 July 2020), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC7540329). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every eviQ claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, the MASCC/ISOO 2020 guideline that S1 tracks, paraphrased because it is CC BY-NC-ND. S2's guideline statements live mostly in Tables 1-3, which were stripped, so only the narrative text is anchored; its photobiomodulation, chlorhexidine and reversed-guideline positions were absent from S1.

claims.claim: **Oral mucositis and stomatitis are different conditions** despite the terms being used loosely: their clinical picture and underlying mechanisms differ.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral mucositis** means red or ulcerated lesions of the mouth lining caused by anticancer drugs, by radiotherapy (above all to the oesophagus or the head and neck), or by high-dose chemotherapy before a blood and marrow transplant (BMT).
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stomatitis** follows targeted therapies such as tyrosine kinase and mTOR inhibitors; its ulcers look like aphthous ulcers. The agreed name for the mTOR form is mTOR inhibitor-associated stomatitis (mIAS).
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **How common:** every patient given head and neck radiotherapy, and over 96% of those given total body irradiation, gets some mucositis; up to 75% after BMT depending on conditioning; about 20-40% on conventional chemotherapy; 10-40% on targeted agents. In a review of 44 mTOR-inhibitor studies, 73.4% developed stomatitis.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Timing:** radiotherapy mucositis starts about two weeks in, peaks at the end of treatment, and can last up to eight weeks after; after BMT it appears around day 5 and lasts 2 to 3 weeks; with chemotherapy it usually starts 2 to 3 weeks in. mIAS appears within 4-5 days and mostly settles within 7-10 days even if the drug continues.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mucositis lesions are irregular in shape and depth with a fibrinous pseudomembrane,** often alongside damage elsewhere in the gut. **mIAS ulcers are small, distinct and ovoid** with a grey-white centre and red halo, and mIAS does not involve the rest of the gut.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use a scale that captures symptoms, signs and function.** Check pain and swallowing (and response to analgesia), redness or ulcers, dry mouth, thick saliva, candida or other infection, aspiration, voice change, taste, eating, hydration, mouth-care adherence, and dentures or piercings.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Grade stomatitis with the mIAS scale, not a chemotherapy/radiotherapy scale** such as CTCAE, which can mismeasure targeted-therapy stomatitis.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral mucositis also brings eating and swallowing problems, tube or intravenous feeding, more opioid use and interrupted cancer treatment;** in immunosuppressed patients it is linked with bacteraemia, longer admissions and higher mortality at 100 days.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mucositis is dangerous as well as painful:** it is a significant risk factor for febrile neutropenia, can threaten the airway, and can lead to sepsis during post-BMT aplasia.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Good basic mouth care underpins prevention and limits severity of both conditions:** teach oral hygiene, remove trauma sources such as poorly fitting dentures, and avoid hard or spicy food, hot drinks, smoking and alcohol. Involve a multidisciplinary team.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MASCC/ISOO suggests a structured multi-agent oral care protocol** (set timing, frequency and products for bland rinses, brushing and flossing) to prevent mucositis during chemotherapy, head and neck radiotherapy and HSCT; professional dental care, patient education and saline or bicarbonate rinses rest on expert opinion.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Chlorhexidine is not suggested for preventing mucositis in head and neck radiotherapy,** though it can still be used to treat or prevent an oral infection that coexists with mucositis.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The MASCC/ISOO options are not ranked:** any effective one for the setting is reasonable. Where none is recommended, the mainstays are pain relief, nutritional support and preventing secondary infection.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Saline or bicarbonate rinses:** MASCC/ISOO makes no recommendation either way; plain water rinses are fine if those are not tolerated, to keep patients doing mouth care.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recommended by MASCC/ISOO:** 30 minutes of oral cryotherapy (ice chips) with bolus fluorouracil or high-dose melphalan (with or without TBI) before BMT; and patient-controlled morphine analgesia for pain.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use cryotherapy with oxaliplatin:** cold can worsen its throat and larynx dysaesthesia.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cryotherapy works by constricting surface blood vessels so less drug reaches the mouth;** because cooling is brief, it only suits short infusions or drugs with a short half-life.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Photobiomodulation (low-level laser or light therapy) inside the mouth is recommended to prevent mucositis** in HSCT, in head and neck radiotherapy alone (upgraded from a suggestion in 2014), and in head and neck chemoradiotherapy (new). Each published protocol's settings should be followed exactly, as a whole.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tell patients about possible risks of photobiomodulation:** some authors raise a long-term cancer-promoting effect; long-term follow-up has shown no rise in recurrence, but animal data conflict.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Benzydamine mouthwash (the PBS drug):** MASCC/ISOO recommends it for head and neck radiotherapy up to 50 Gy without chemotherapy, and suggests it with concurrent chemoradiotherapy. In Australia it is routinely available only in an alcohol-based form, is seldom used, and the eviQ head and neck radiation oncology committee advises against it.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suggested for head and neck chemoradiotherapy:** oral glutamine 10-30 g/day throughout treatment for prevention; morphine 0.2% mouthwash for mucositis pain; and honey, topical and oral, may be used for prevention (with or without chemotherapy).
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Caution with glutamine:** the oral glutamine suggestion for head and neck chemoradiotherapy rests on 2 RCTs, and MASCC/ISOO flags that 1 HSCT study of intravenous glutamine reported more relapse and deaths.
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Downgraded in this update to 'no guideline possible':** doxepin mouthwash and transdermal fentanyl (previously suggested), zinc for head and neck radiotherapy, misoprostol mouthwash, and sucralfate to prevent chemotherapy mucositis. Chewing gum is suggested against for preventing mucositis in children on chemotherapy (it is fine for other reasons).
claims.locator: Elad S, Cheng KKF, Lalla RV, Yarom N, et al., Mucositis Study Group of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and International Society of Oral Oncology (MASCC/ISOO), Cancer 2020;126(19):4423-4431 (doi 10.1002/cncr.33100), 'MASCC/ISOO clinical practice guidelines for the management of mucositis secondary to cancer therapy', published online 28 July 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540329/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recommended against:** intravenous glutamine to prevent mucositis in BMT, and sucralfate for mucositis pain in head and neck radiotherapy or solid-tumour chemotherapy.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lower the oral-cavity radiation dose where technique allows,** since that dose drives mucositis risk.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevention:** use saline rather than plain-water rinses (higher infection risk on targeted agents, expert opinion); a steroid mouthwash lowers the incidence and severity of mIAS.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment (expert opinion):** rinse more often, up to hourly; sugar-free gum or saliva substitutes for dryness; anaesthetic rinses such as viscous lidocaine 2% or coating agents for mild to moderate pain; topical or systemic analgesia (transdermal fentanyl plus short-acting opioid for breakthrough has worked); dexamethasone mouth rinse for lesions; and oral prednisolone or intralesional triamcinolone for very symptomatic ulcers.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tell patients to report straight away** any pain, trouble swallowing, thrush, mouth ulcers, bleeding or difficulty speaking, and to check their mouth every day.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Daily mouth care:** see a dentist before treatment if possible; keep the mouth moist; use a water-based lip balm (not paraffin or petroleum jelly); brush with a soft brush four times a day with mild fluoride toothpaste, replacing it monthly; rinse with alcohol-free mouthwash; keep flossing only if already a habit; clean dentures separately; avoid smoking, alcohol, acidic, hot, spicy, rough or fizzy foods and drinks.
claims.locator: eviQ, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Oral mucositis and stomatitis (ID 210, v.5)', last reviewed 5 February 2021 (review due 30 June 2023; page marked 'Under review'), https://www.eviq.org.au/clinical-resources/side-effect-and-toxicity-management/oropharyngeal/210-oral-mucositis-and-stomatitis, retrieved 2026-09-23
